entities.summary:
The University of Chicago, founded in 1890 with a gift from oil magnate John D. Rockefeller, is the only research university in history to have created two entirely new academic disciplines — economics (the Chicago School) and sociology (the Chicago School of Sociology) — while simultaneously transforming law through the Law and Economics movement and philosophy through Pragmatism and logical positivism. The University's 100 Nobel laureates (the most per enrolled student of any university) and the Chicago School economic theories that governed global free-market policy from 1970-2008 make it the most intellectually influential university of the 20th century.

Rockefeller's 1890 gift established the university on Frederick Law Olmsted's Gothic campus in Hyde Park. The first president, William Rainey Harper, created the quarter system and emphasized research over teaching — establishing the research university model. The 1942 Chicago Pile-1 nuclear reactor under Stagg Field — constructed by Enrico Fermi's team including 49 scientists — created the first artificial self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction on December 2, 1942, enabling the Manhattan Project.

Milton Friedman's Chicago School economics — monetarism, free-market anti-Keynesian theory, privatization — became the intellectual foundation for Reagan-Thatcher economic policy, the 'Washington Consensus' imposed on developing countries by the IMF, and the Chilean 'Chicago Boys' economic reforms under Pinochet. The Chicago School's global influence from 1970-2008 transformed economic governance in 50+ countries. Gary Becker's application of economic analysis to marriage, crime, and discrimination created 'economics imperialism' — the extension of economic methodology into all social sciences.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The University of Chicago created the first nuclear chain reaction (enabling atomic weapons and nuclear power), the Chicago School economics (governing global free-market policy for 40 years), and 100 Nobel laureates — making it the most consequential research university in 20th-century science and economics.
